newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST -Swedish Riksbank to cut repo on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST -Swedish Riksbank to cut repo on Tuesday.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, is expected to cut its key repo rate by another 10 basis points to 5.05 percent at its weekly tender on Tuesday, a Reuter poll of six analysts said on Monday.
This would be the 20th cut this year to the repo rate, the central rate in the bank's three-tier system and a key tool for controlling money market liquidity.
"I think it will be lowered by 10 basis points. There is no reason for the Riksbank to change its policy of lowering the rate," said Nordbanken analysts Tomas Pousette.
The repo rate, which began the year at 8.91 percent, was last cut on September 10 when the Riksbank trimmed 10 basis points to 5.15 percent.
It was the first time the bank had cut the repo by 10 basis points, previously cutting 15 basis points each move and earlier in the year, by larger amounts.
The other two elements of the corridor, the deposit and lending rates, are currently set at 4.75 percent and 6.25 percent, respectively.
Analysts expected the bank to continue cutting the repo rate in 10 basis-point steps.
Pousette said one reason to continue lowering the rate was that the Riksbank did not want to see a quick strengthening of the crown.
"We at Nordbanken, think the Riksbank will lower the repo rate several more times until it reaches 4.60 percent," he said.
A recent Reuters poll found analysts on average expected the repo rate to be reduced to 4.69 percent over the next three months.
After that, analysts forecast the Riksbank would start to raise the repo rate.
